A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, renamed from ubGen to lbGen. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original transfer-learning, detection, segmentation, bias-evaluation, and ablation results for models pretrained on its generated data.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports computational costs in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The SD1.5/LoRA procedure, CLIP-based dataset and individual-image alignment, Q-ALIGN quality loss, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Renaming ubGen to lbGen does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet-based pretraining, eight transfer-learning datasets, COCO, ADE20K, and shape, context, and background bias evaluations. Adding more categories is discussed only as a possible extension.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain IN-Real, IN-SD1.5, IN-GenRobust, and IN-RealFake as comparators. Table 4 retains the same ImageNet-100 controls and ablation configurations.

E3.justification: The backbone configurations, evaluation metrics, reduced-data settings, splits, and training and generation hyperparameters remain unchanged, including Tables 5–8. The newly disclosed image count and computing resources do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The specific-bias tests, reduced-data evaluations, loss-component ablations, CLIP-capacity comparison, and polysemy examples are retained. Expanded ablation explanations and limitations introduce no additional tests or analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The point-estimate tables and plots retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the benchmark plots retain their numerical results and findings. Appendix F newly reports approximately 1 hour of generator fine-tuning and 52 hours to generate about 1.3 million images using 8 A100 GPUs, adding limited computational results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same mathematical content, including the losses, reinforcement-learning formulation, and scoring expressions. The added prose definition of dataset bias and revised bias terminology introduce no formal mathematical definition, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, and conclusion replace unbiased generation with low-biased generation, moderating the central claim. The proposed contribution and claims of improved downstream generalization otherwise remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 defines dataset bias in terms of impaired generalization and expands Appendix G to acknowledge residual bias from limited category coverage and scarce fine-grained categories. It proposes adding categories as a mitigation, while retaining the existing polysemy and applicability limitations.

D1.justification: New Appendix F discloses GPU hardware, fine-tuning and generation times, and approximate generated-dataset size. The code link changes from the ubGen repository path to lbGen; existing implementation and hyperparameter details remain.

R1.justification: The same 63 references and the same positioning against bias-measurement work and ImageNet-mimicking synthesis are retained. Reference 48 is repositioned within an existing introductory argument, without a substantive change in the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and method terminology throughout, adds a bias-definition footnote, and makes localized explanatory edits. Computing Resources becomes Appendix F and Limitation moves to G; the main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Existing graphics receive naming, formatting, and cropping adjustments. Figure 4 and Figure 7 change columns, and Table 2 moves from page 6 to page 7. The seven figures and eight tables retain their basic content and structure.

improvement.justification: v2 moderates the central unbiased-generation claim and explicitly acknowledges remaining category-coverage limitations in Appendix G. Hardware and runtime disclosures in Appendix F improve practical transparency. These changes improve the calibration and documentation of an otherwise unchanged method and benchmark study.
